english: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be three mutually independent events such that $P(A)=\dfrac12$, the probability that at least one of $A$, $B$, $C$ occurs is $0.85$, and the probability that exactly one of $A$, $B$, $C$ occurs is $0.4$. Then the probability that exactly two of $A$, $B$, $C$ occur is ______.
hindi: माना $A$, $B$ तथा $C$ तीन परस्पर स्वतंत्र घटनाएँ हैं, जिनके लिए $P(A)=\dfrac12$ है, $A$, $B$, $C$ में से कम से कम एक घटना के घटित होने की प्रायिकता $0.85$ है, तथा $A$, $B$, $C$ में से ठीक एक घटना के घटित होने की प्रायिकता $0.4$ है। तब $A$, $B$, $C$ में से ठीक दो घटनाओं के घटित होने की प्रायिकता ______ है।
solution: Let $P(B)=b,\ P(C)=c$. At least one $=1-P(A'B'C')$: $\dfrac12(1-b)(1-c)=0.15\Rightarrow b+c-bc=0.7$
The four cases none / exactly one / exactly two / all three have total probability $1$
solution_full: Let $P(B)=b$ and $P(C)=c$. By independence, the complements $A'$, $B'$, $C'$ are also independent.
At least one of the events occurs is the complement of none occurring: $1-P(A'\cap B'\cap C')=0.85$, so $P(A')P(B')P(C')=\dfrac12(1-b)(1-c)=0.15$, that is, $(1-b)(1-c)=0.3$, or $b+c-bc=0.7$.
Exactly one occurs: either $A$ occurs and neither $B$ nor $C$, or $A$ fails and exactly one of $B$, $C$ occurs.
Subtracting from $b+c-bc=0.7$ gives $bc=0.2$, and then $b+c=0.9$; so $\{b,c\}=\{0.4,0.5\}$ (roots of $t^2-0.9t+0.2=0$), both valid probabilities.
All three occur: $P(A\cap B\cap C)=\dfrac12\cdot bc=0.1$.
Check: none $+$ exactly one $+$ exactly two $+$ all three $=0.15+0.4+0.35+0.1=1$.
originality_note: New: one probability known and two unknown; the 'at least one' value (through its complement) and the 'exactly one' value give the symmetric functions b + c - bc and b + c - 2bc, and the 'exactly two' probability follows without needing b and c separately (way 5: link between the exactly-one / exactly-two decomposition of three sets and complementary events). Closest known: the JEE problem with independent E1, E2, E3 and given probabilities of exactly one, exactly two and none (alpha, beta, gamma, p). Different because: here P(A) is given, 'at least one' replaces 'none' in the data, and the unknown is the exactly-two probability via the partition none / one / two / three.

key_step: Turning 'at least one = 0.85' into (1-b)(1-c) = 0.3 and 'exactly one = 0.4' into b + c - 2bc = 0.5, then bc = 0.2.
justification: Two linked ideas: complement for 'at least one' and the exactly-one decomposition, giving a symmetric system; then exactly two by the partition. Numerical answer without options. Comparable to 2021-P1-Q13 (L3) and 2024-P2-Q9 (L3) probability manipulations.

concept_use.Elements in exactly one / exactly two of: P(exactly one) and P(exactly two) are written as sums over the Venn regions of A, B, C (A only, B only, C only; pairs without the third).
concept_use.Complementary events and 'at least one': P(at least one) = 1 - P(A' B' C') = 0.85 gives (1-b)(1-c) = 0.3, and the partition none / one / two / three gives exactly two = 1 - 0.15 - 0.4 - 0.1.
